copy.blurb:
Senegal face Iraq on Friday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — one of the widest in the priced field on the Senegal side, +18.7pp.

Elo numbers going in: Senegal 1790, Iraq 1540. That's a 250-point lead for Senegal — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Senegal to win at 69%, the draw at 15%, and Iraq to win at 16%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Senegal on the win side reads 69%.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Senegal to win at 50%, the draw at 24%, and Iraq to win at 12%. The Senegal side trades at 50% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of −100. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 69%, +18.7pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Senegal, that haircut lands the model at 61%; the market is at 50%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +10.7pp. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Senegal priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 35 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Senegal a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.
The +18.7pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Senegal side, not a blanket read on the market.
copy.summary: Senegal are favourites on the market at 50% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 69%, a +18.7pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
copy.title: Senegal v Iraq · the model leans Senegal
